A1.evidence: Row 6 entitlement: HTTPS delivery from the article landing page. The pack shows the article DOI resolves (http_status 200). The paper's own analysis script is reachable this way.

A1_1.evidence: HTTPS is open, free, and universally implementable. The article is 'an open access article under the CC BY license' (p.1).

A1_2.evidence: Fully open resource needing no authentication (open-access article supplement). The v2.1 A1.2 open-case rule applies.

A2.evidence: Row 6: A2 = 0 for supplement-only deposits. There is no independent metadata record to persist.

F1.evidence: Scripts are distributed as supplements of the article under the article DOI: 'The script used to run all validation analyses is available in the supplementary information' (p.4), and the same for the case study tests (p.6); 'Supplementary data ... https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jas.2023.105921' (p.18). The v2.1 F1 granularity rule credits supplements carried under the article DOI.

F2.evidence: The script is a supplement only, with no independent deposit. Row 6 rules out an independent metadata record (F2=0).

F3.evidence: Row 6: supplement-only deposit, so no artefact-level metadata record carries an identifier (F3=0). The pack identifier is the article's Crossref record.

F4.evidence: Row 6: no registry indexing for supplement-only deposits (F4=0). No Zenodo, Software Heritage, or CRAN deposit is mentioned.

I1.evidence: 'All analyses were undertaken in 'R' version 4.3.0. The script used to run all validation analyses is available in the supplementary information' (p.4). R source code is a formal, shared, broadly implementable language.

I2.evidence: No vocabulary or metadata standard is referenced for the software.

I3.evidence: No PID-qualified references to dependencies or input datasets. Only 'R version 4.3.0' is named, with no package citations or identifiers.

R1.evidence: The paper describes in detail what the script does: k values 5, 10, 20, and 30; subsampling at 5/10/20/50% (archaic points 20-50%); 1000 iterations with median values; T_E and 95% T_CI outputs; duplicate removal; and the resampling with sd 0.001 for microliths (s2.3.3, s2.4.1.6.1).

R1_1.evidence: The script is a publisher-hosted supplement, so the article licence extends to it. The paper states CC BY (p.1). The pack records cc-by-4.0 and licence_conflicts conflict=false for the declared supplement, with paper_asserted 'CC BY'. The Elsevier TDM licence URIs in the pack are text-and-data-mining terms, not a more restrictive licence conflicting with CC BY.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is documented: software environment 'R version 4.3.0' (p.4); analysis parameters and workflow (s2.3.3); and authorship of the analysis in the CRediT statement ('Alastair Key: ... Formal analysis'; 'Ivan Jarić: Formal analysis, Methodology').

R1_3.evidence: No package structure, CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, or community review (CRAN, JOSS, rOpenSci) is mentioned. The script is a plain supplementary file.

barriers: Raw morphometric records for the replica handaxe (n=500) and replica Early Archaic point (n=45) assemblages are not stated to be shared. The archaic points 'have not been used in any other published studies'. Tier 4 from the paper's statements.

Old Park flakes, Boxgrove handaxes, Sibudu bipolar cores, capuchin flakes, and geometric microliths: prior studies are cited for collection methods only, and no data source or identifier is given. Tier 3/4.
Olduvai cleavers come from Martín-Ramos (2022), an unpublished PhD thesis. Tier 3.
Copper socketed tang points (n=93): no source or availability is given. Tier 4.
Middle Historic bowls (Petrie 2020) and Neolithic pots (Robb 2007) are tied to monographs. Tier 3 (closed monograph or co-author held).
The eight Acheulean handaxe assemblages from Key (2015) in Fig. 6 come from an unpublished PhD thesis. Tier 3.

Paleoindian points: 'Data are derived from Buchanan and Hamilton's (2021) study'. This is a published source, credited generously as Tier 2; the paper does not confirm that raw data are retrievable there.

A1.evidence: Data-completeness coverage is minimal (1/13 datasets reachable at Tier 0-2, 7.7%), so the A1 cross-reference sets A1 = 0. No ethical restriction is documented.

A1_1.evidence: Only the Paleoindian data have a reachable path, through the cited Buchanan and Hamilton (2021) publication, and the paper never shows they are retrievable by an open protocol. Conjunctive over principal datasets: 0.

A1_2.evidence: No principal dataset is an open resource, and no access-control mechanism is documented. Unpublished thesis and monograph data are closed with no stated justification.

A2.evidence: No repository or metadata persistence commitment exists for any principal dataset.

F1.evidence: The paper gives no PID for any principal morphometric dataset. The supplement is described only as Supplementary Tables 1-3 and Figs 1-3 plus scripts, and the paper never states that raw data sit in the supplement under the article DOI. Principal datasets include an unpublished thesis (Martín-Ramos 2022) and never-published archaic points. Conjunctive rule: 0.

F2.evidence: No independent metadata record exists for any principal dataset. Even supplement-only deposit gets F2=0 under Row 6.

F3.evidence: No dataset metadata record carries an identifier. The pack's only record is the article's Crossref record.

F4.evidence: No principal dataset is indexed in a searchable registry.

I1.evidence: The only data in the paper are descriptive summaries and OLE result tables in PDF (Tables 1-7). Raw records are in no structured format.

I2.evidence: No controlled vocabularies or ontologies are referenced for the data.

I3.evidence: No PID-qualified links from the data to source datasets. Sources are cited as literature only (e.g. 'Data are derived from Buchanan and Hamilton's (2021) study').

R1.evidence: No dataset-level documentation (README or data dictionary) for any principal dataset. The paper describes variables and units (Tables 5-7 captions) but the data themselves are not shared.

R1_1.evidence: No licence identified for any principal dataset. The article's CC BY licence covers the article and its supplement, but the paper never says raw data are in the supplement.

R1_2.evidence: Provenance is partly given in the text: excavation context and collection-method citations (e.g. 'methods used to collect these data are described in Key and Lycett (2017)'). For copper socketed tang points (n=93), no collection source is given. Conjunctive rule: 0.

R1_3.evidence: No deposit-level community standard (DataCite, Dublin Core, or a domain schema) and no accredited domain repository.
